answers.how: The ball diameter is approximately 36 px, giving 0.21/36 m per pixel. A quadratic fit to its pre-impact center positions gives approximately 541 px/s at 0.5 s.
A quadratic fit to the pre-impact motion gives a deceleration magnitude of approximately 63 px/s². Multiplying by 0.21/36 m per pixel gives approximately 0.37 m/s².
The fitted ball motion gives approximately 510 px/s at 1 s. Using the diameter scale, 510 × 0.21/36 is approximately 2.98 m/s.
The pre-impact trajectory is consistent with approximately constant deceleration. Its fitted magnitude is approximately 63 × 0.21/36 = 0.37 m/s².
An upright pin measures approximately 57 px tall, compared with the ball's approximately 36 px diameter: 57 × 0.21/36 ≈ 0.33 m.
The fully visible foreground black return opening measures approximately 50 px vertically: 50 × 0.21/36 ≈ 0.29 m.
